tasks.short: Enter and maintain supplier and customer transactions in AFAS, then check the balances.

today.trigger: An approved invoice, credit note or transaction file arrives.
steps: Collect documents and exports from Outlook, AFAS and agency portals.
Find the supplier or customer and check the accounting period.
Enter or import the transaction into AFAS.
Attach supporting documents and check the resulting balances.
drudgery: Copying the same references between files and AFAS
today.time_sinks: Repeated entry and import corrections across three sites; the actual split between manual entry and existing automation needs confirmation.

lenses.faster: Import approved transactions through validated mappings and attach their source documents automatically. Repeated typing and routine balance checks disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A new approved transaction starts validation and posting; failed checks enter an exception queue. Automatic posting is restricted to approved sources, mappings and open periods.
lenses.ambitious: Keep transaction backlogs visible throughout the month so missing records are resolved before close. Give each site a daily view of unprocessed finance documents.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive entry and searching for attachments. Keep the investigation of unusual transactions and conversations that resolve them.
lenses.options: Test alternative import mappings against historical transactions before changing production rules. Compare rejection rates and corrections required.
lenses.altitude: Own the posting rules, source quality and exception queue instead of operating every entry screen.
reach: Prepare routine reconciliation inputs for the accountants
Investigate finance data quality issues with the Controller

tasks.human_edge: Recognise transactions that do not reflect the underlying business event and challenge incomplete or misleading evidence.
tasks.pattern_why: Validated imports, required fields, period checks and approved mappings can run as ordinary software; a model is unnecessary for structured records.

in_practice.trigger: An approved document or structured transaction file reaches the controlled intake location.
steps: Validate source, approval, supplier or customer, required fields and duplicate identifiers.
Apply approved mappings and reject closed periods or unsupported transaction types.
Post eligible records through a supported AFAS interface and link their documents.
Reconcile source counts and amounts to accepted, rejected and posted records.
Route exceptions to the bookkeeper with a clear reason and retain a retry history.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper resolves exceptions; the Accountant approves new accounting mappings. Supplier bank changes and payment release follow separate approval controls.
systems: Proposed scheduled import and validation service
data_needed: Approved source transactions and attachments
AFAS master data and supported interface specifications
Approved posting mappings and period status
Existing transaction identifiers and approval records
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS transaction history and a restricted SharePoint import register recording source IDs, rule versions, outcomes and exception decisions.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit provides financial administration for recording purchase and sales transactions; the available import interfaces depend on configuration.
The proposed workflow, 65% human time saving and 2.5 times end-to-end speedup are untested planning assumptions for Noordhaven.

risks: An incorrect mapping could repeat the same error across many transactions.
Retries could create duplicates unless every source record has a stable identifier.
An integration account could bypass approval or period controls if permissions are too broad.
research_questions: What proportion of these hours is manual entry, import correction or analysis today?
Which supported AFAS interfaces are available, and do they preserve approvals and attachment links?
What proportion of records passes all checks without human correction in a representative pilot?

tasks.short: Check invoice figures, AFAS postings and supporting documents for mistakes before they affect the accounts.

today.trigger: An invoice or posting needs checking, or a close review identifies a possible error.
steps: Retrieve the invoice, posting and available order or approval evidence.
Recalculate totals, VAT and quantities and compare references.
Check ledger codes, site allocation, accounting period and possible duplicates.
Correct errors or ask the responsible colleague for evidence.
drudgery: Comparing invoice lines with exported records
Repeating the same checks across agency invoices
today.time_sinks: Locating evidence and separating real discrepancies from formatting differences.

lenses.faster: Check arithmetic, duplicates, codes and available order evidence automatically. Show the exact field or line that failed instead of asking the bookkeeper to inspect every document.
lenses.autonomous: Each new posting runs through a versioned control set. Clean records pass the check stage and exceptions wait for investigation.
lenses.ambitious: Check every eligible transaction throughout the month instead of relying on occasional samples. Identify recurring errors by supplier, site and process.
lenses.joy: Remove line-by-line comparison and calculator work. Leave the bookkeeper with explanations to investigate and errors worth preventing.
lenses.options: Compare strict and more permissive matching tolerances on past data. Choose the setting that catches material errors without flooding the queue.
lenses.altitude: Design and improve the transaction controls, including how missed errors and false alarms are measured.
reach: Prepare control evidence for the Accountant
Support the Controller's recurring-error analysis

tasks.human_edge: Judge whether a formally valid invoice represents a real service and whether conflicting evidence needs escalation.
tasks.pattern_why: Arithmetic, duplicate detection and approved code checks are explicit and testable; document extraction can be added separately where inputs are unstructured.

in_practice.trigger: A new invoice or posting becomes available for validation.
steps: Read transaction fields and retrieve linked approval, order and service evidence where available.
Run deterministic arithmetic, VAT, duplicate, period and code checks.
For agency invoices, compare approved hours and contracted rates, including explicitly agreed allowances.
Record passed checks and send failures to a queue with source references.
Have the bookkeeper resolve discrepancies and escalate accounting or contract questions.
in_practice.human_gate: Failed checks require resolution before the record passes validation; the Accountant approves control-rule changes and material corrections.
data_needed: Invoice lines and AFAS postings
Approved orders, service confirmations and agency hours where available
Approved agency rate schedules and applicable allowance agreements
VAT rules, accounting mappings and materiality thresholds
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted control register linked to AFAS document IDs, with check results, rule versions, evidence and reviewer decisions.

evidence.claim: Excel Power Query supports joining datasets and isolating unmatched rows for reconciliation checks.
The proposed control coverage, 70% human time saving and three times end-to-end speedup have not been tested at Noordhaven.

risks: Missing order or service evidence could make reliable matching impossible.
Incorrect VAT or agency allowance rules could create systematic errors.
Too many low-value alerts could cause reviewers to overlook significant discrepancies.
research_questions: Which checks already run in AFAS, and which still require manual work?
Are approved agency hours and contracted rates available at invoice-line level?
On historical transactions, how many known errors are detected and how many clean records are flagged?
Who approves changes when contracts, CAO-related allowances or VAT treatment change?

tasks.short: Assign ledger, VAT and site codes to invoices and other accounting documents.

today.trigger: A document arrives without complete or reliable accounting codes.
steps: Read the document and identify the supplier, service and relevant period.
Find comparable postings and the current coding guidance.
Choose ledger, VAT and site codes.
Enter the codes and ask the budget holder or Accountant about uncertain cases.
drudgery: Searching old invoices for a usable example
today.time_sinks: Ambiguous descriptions, mixed-service invoices and inconsistent historical coding.

lenses.faster: Suggest codes from the document, approved policy and relevant examples, with the supporting passage shown. Apply approved supplier rules directly where the meaning is unambiguous.
lenses.autonomous: Document receipt produces a coding proposal and flags missing information. The bookkeeper approves the proposal before it becomes an accounting entry.
lenses.ambitious: Code costs consistently across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo so site comparisons need fewer manual repairs. Detect recurring gaps in supplier descriptions.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive lookups and copying from old postings. Keep the judgement about what the cost actually represents.
lenses.options: Show up to three plausible treatments for ambiguous documents and explain what evidence would distinguish them. Do not invent an allocation when the source lacks one.
lenses.altitude: Maintain the coding policy, approved examples and exception categories that guide future proposals.
reach: Prepare cost classification reviews for the Accountant
Improve site cost data with the FP&A Analysts

tasks.human_edge: Resolve business purpose, capital-versus-expense questions and uncertain VAT treatment with the people accountable for them.
tasks.pattern_why: A model can interpret invoice descriptions and propose structured codes, while deterministic checks constrain valid values and a person approves the accounting treatment.

in_practice.trigger: An uncoded document enters the intake queue.
steps: Extract document text and identify supplier, service, dates and explicit site references.
Retrieve current coding guidance and approved examples within the user's access rights.
Propose valid codes with source evidence and flag ambiguous allocations.
Validate codes, required dimensions and arithmetic against AFAS configuration.
Let the bookkeeper approve or amend the proposal before writing it to AFAS.
in_practice.human_gate: Every model-generated coding proposal is approved by the bookkeeper; policy exceptions and material judgement go to the Accountant.
systems: Proposed document extraction and language-model service
data_needed: Invoice text and attachments
Current chart of accounts, VAT codes and site dimensions
Approved coding policy and reviewed examples
Budget-holder explanations for ambiguous services
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted coding register containing document IDs, retrieved policy versions, proposed codes, reviewer changes and final AFAS references.

evidence.claim: Language models can propose structured classifications from document text, but accounting accuracy depends on supplied policy and validation.
A 50% human time saving and 1.8 times end-to-end speedup are untested assumptions for this coding workflow.

risks: Historical postings may teach the system inconsistent or incorrect treatment.
A plausible explanation may hide an unsupported ledger or VAT choice.
Invoice text may contain malicious instructions; it must be treated as data.
Personal information in documents requires restricted access and an AVG/GDPR-compliant processing arrangement.
research_questions: How often do experienced bookkeepers agree on the codes for the same document?
What proportion of documents follows stable supplier rules versus requiring business judgement?
Does a blind historical test reduce review time without increasing accounting corrections?
Can the selected service meet Noordhaven's data access, retention and processing requirements?

tasks.short: Calculate invoice balances, discounts and interest using the agreed terms.

today.trigger: A payment, customer query, overdue balance or adjustment requires a calculation.
steps: Retrieve the balance, credit notes, payment history and relevant terms.
Check dates, applicable rates and discount conditions.
Calculate the amount in AFAS or Excel.
Check the result and document the calculation for review or use.
today.time_sinks: Finding the authoritative terms and reconstructing changes after credits or partial payments.

lenses.faster: Pull balances and approved terms directly into tested calculation rules. Recalculation and an itemised explanation become automatic.
lenses.autonomous: A balance or terms change recalculates affected amounts. Unsupported terms and disputed balances become exceptions.
lenses.ambitious: Calculate the financial effect of payment timing across all eligible invoices. Make discount opportunities and interest exposure visible before deadlines.
lenses.joy: Remove formula copying and repeated arithmetic. Keep the work of resolving disputed terms and explaining unusual balances.
lenses.options: Compare payment today, on the due date and after a proposed delay, using explicit assumptions. Show discount and interest effects separately.
lenses.altitude: Own a tested library of calculation rules and the approved terms behind them.
reach: Prepare balance calculations for the Credit and Collections Officer
Provide payment-timing inputs to the FP&A Analysts

tasks.human_edge: Determine which terms legitimately apply and when a calculation should lead to a commercial discussion rather than an automatic charge.
tasks.pattern_why: Financial arithmetic should use tested decimal calculations and explicit terms, with no model generating or executing the numerical logic at runtime.

in_practice.trigger: An eligible balance changes or a user requests a calculation.
steps: Retrieve current balances, payment allocations, dates and approved terms.
Select the applicable versioned calculation rule or flag unsupported terms.
Calculate with explicit day-count, rounding and partial-payment rules.
Store an itemised result and route disputed or unusual cases for review.
in_practice.human_gate: The Accountant approves calculation rules and changes; the authorised colleague decides whether to issue interest, grant a discount or amend contractual terms.
data_needed: Open items, credits and allocated payments
Approved contracts and payment terms
Effective interest rates and discount conditions
Day-count, currency and rounding policies
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted calculation register recording input snapshots, effective terms, rule versions, results and any approved overrides.

evidence.claim: Excel provides date and financial functions that support repeatable balance, discount and interest calculations when the terms are explicit.
An 80% human time saving and four times end-to-end speedup are untested assumptions; missing terms could substantially reduce them.

risks: The wrong rate, effective date or day-count convention can produce a precise but incorrect result.
Unallocated receipts can overstate overdue balances and interest.
A calculated amount may be mistaken for authorisation to charge or pay it.
research_questions: Which calculations actually occur in this role, and how much time does each consume?
Are contractual terms available as approved structured data?
Do results match reviewed examples covering credits, partial payments, rate changes and rounding?
Which calculations already run correctly in AFAS?

tasks.short: Prepare Rabobank payment batches for approved supplier invoices, utilities and tax obligations.

today.trigger: A payment run is due or an approved obligation reaches its payment deadline.
steps: Collect approved invoices and payment instructions, including reviewed tax amounts.
Check due dates, credits, payment blocks and beneficiary details.
Prepare a payment proposal in AFAS and resolve discrepancies.
Submit the batch for authorised review and Rabobank release.
Check the bank response and record rejected or completed payments.
drudgery: Checking the same payment fields repeatedly
today.time_sinks: Missing approvals, beneficiary discrepancies and urgent requests close to bank cutoffs; Dutch payment batches replace the O*NET reference to checks.

lenses.faster: Assemble a payment proposal from approved obligations and show only blocks, changes and exceptions for review. Attach the supporting evidence automatically.
lenses.autonomous: The payment calendar triggers draft preparation and approval reminders. Bank submission and release remain subject to the payment mandate.
lenses.ambitious: Make upcoming obligations and missing approvals visible before each payment run. Reduce avoidable late fees and last-minute payment requests.
lenses.joy: Remove approval chasing and repeated field comparisons. Keep cash judgement, fraud challenge and accountable review.
lenses.options: Present pay-on-due-date, discount-taking and cash-preserving proposals with their consequences. Never silently defer taxes or other fixed obligations.
lenses.altitude: Manage the quality and reliability of payment preparation instead of assembling every batch by hand.
reach: Prepare short-term cash outflow inputs for the FP&A Analysts
Maintain payment control evidence for the Accountant

tasks.human_edge: Challenge suspicious requests, verify beneficiary changes independently and apply cash priorities under the Finance Director's authority.
tasks.pattern_why: Preparation spans obligations, approvals, exceptions and bank responses; deterministic checks support the workflow, but named people approve the batch and release funds.

in_practice.trigger: A scheduled payment run starts or an authorised urgent-payment request is received.
steps: Collect approved open items and separately approved tax payment instructions.
Check duplicates, credits, blocks, due dates and beneficiary changes against controlled master data.
Prepare a draft batch and summary of totals, exceptions and differences from the previous proposal.
Obtain batch approval and release through Rabobank under the required segregation of duties.
Reconcile bank acceptance and execution statuses to AFAS and investigate rejects.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper reviews the proposal; authorised approvers approve and release the exact batch under the bank mandate. Any subsequent batch change requires renewed approval.
data_needed: Approved open items and reviewed tax instructions
Controlled beneficiary master data
Payment blocks, credits and due dates
Payment mandate, approval limits and bank statuses
Finance-approved cash priorities
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS payment records, Rabobank authorisation history and a restricted batch register identifying the approved batch version and its supporting evidence.

evidence.claim: Rabobank business banking supports payment batches and payment authorisation; Noordhaven's channels and mandate must be verified.
The proposed preparation workflow, 45% human time saving and 1.5 times end-to-end speedup are untested assumptions.

risks: A fraudulent beneficiary change could pass ordinary invoice checks.
A modified batch could differ from the batch that reviewers approved.
Resubmission after an unclear bank response could duplicate payments.
Approval delays and bank cutoffs may limit elapsed-time improvement.
research_questions: Which AFAS-to-Rabobank payment functions are already configured?
Can approval be tied to the exact batch contents and invalidated after any change?
How are beneficiary changes independently verified and separated from payment preparation?
How much payment-run time is preparation versus waiting for approval or bank execution?

tasks.short: Reconcile AFAS transactions with Excel registers, bank statements and agency records.

today.trigger: A daily check or close deadline requires two records to agree.
steps: Export the relevant AFAS ledger or transaction report.
Collect the corresponding Excel register, bank statement or agency record.
Align dates, references, signs and amounts and mark matched items.
Investigate differences and document corrections or outstanding items.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same reconciliation each period
today.time_sinks: Inconsistent references, timing differences and spreadsheet versions; the presence of manual journals needs confirmation.

lenses.faster: Normalise source files and match exact references and amounts automatically. Start with the unmatched items and a complete control total.
lenses.autonomous: Arrival of both source files starts the reconciliation. Missing files and unresolved differences generate an exception with an owner.
lenses.ambitious: Reconcile critical accounts daily so close contains fewer surprises. Identify manual registers that can be retired once their purpose is covered.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet preparation and repetitive ticking. Keep the detective work of explaining real differences.
lenses.options: Compare exact matching with approved date windows or grouped matches on historical records. Show how each rule changes unresolved balances and false matches.
lenses.altitude: Own reconciliation coverage, matching rules and the age of unresolved differences.
reach: Prepare balance-sheet reconciliation schedules for the accountants
Support the Controller's close-readiness reporting

tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a legitimate timing difference from an omitted, duplicated or incorrectly recorded business event.
tasks.pattern_why: File normalisation, exact and approved grouped matching, control totals and exception ageing are explicit rules with checkable outputs.

in_practice.trigger: The required source files for a reconciliation period become available.
steps: Validate file identity, period, completeness and source totals.
Normalise identifiers, dates, currency, signs and decimal formats without changing the originals.
Apply approved matching rules and prevent records from being matched twice.
Produce matched totals, unmatched items and differences against each source.
Assign unresolved differences and publish the reconciliation for review.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper investigates unmatched items; the Accountant signs off close reconciliations and approves journals separately. Matching alone never creates a balancing entry.
data_needed: Complete source files and control totals
Stable references, amounts, dates and currencies
Approved matching tolerances and grouping rules
Prior unresolved items and their owners
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint reconciliation library retaining source versions, matching-rule versions, matched record IDs, differences and sign-offs.

evidence.claim: Excel Power Query supports repeatable transformations, dataset merges and anti-joins for unmatched records.
A 75% human time saving and three times end-to-end speedup depend on source quality and remain untested at Noordhaven.

risks: Incomplete source files could produce an apparently clean reconciliation.
Loose matching tolerances could conceal real errors.
Grouped matches could reuse transactions or hide offsetting differences without explicit controls.
research_questions: Which manual journals or Excel registers actually exist, and why are they maintained?
Do both sides contain stable identifiers and reliable completeness totals?
How much historical reconciliation effort concerns matching versus investigating differences?
Can the rules reproduce reviewed reconciliations without hiding any known discrepancies?

tasks.short: Answer supplier, customer and colleague questions using AFAS records and supporting documents.

today.trigger: A question arrives about an invoice, payment, credit or account balance.
steps: Identify the requester, account and exact question.
Search AFAS and retrieve supporting documents or correspondence.
Check recent transactions and explain any timing differences.
Send an answer or refer disputes and sensitive questions to the responsible colleague.
drudgery: Searching several places for the same invoice
today.time_sinks: Unclear references and checking whether a dashboard or transaction status is current.

lenses.faster: Retrieve permitted records and draft an answer with invoice references, source links and an as-of time. The bookkeeper checks the evidence instead of assembling it.
lenses.autonomous: An incoming question creates a draft response when the requester and account can be identified. Ambiguous identity, stale data or missing evidence stops drafting and prompts investigation.
lenses.ambitious: Offer consistent, traceable answers and identify recurring questions caused by poor invoice information. Feed those causes back into the process.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated searches and boilerplate writing. Keep the conversations that resolve confusion or rebuild trust.
lenses.options: Offer a short status reply or a detailed balance explanation from the same verified facts. Show alternative interpretations when a reference matches several records.
lenses.altitude: Own the quality, access rules and freshness of finance answers.
reach: Prepare factual account briefings for the Credit and Collections Officer
Create recurring-question summaries for the Controller

tasks.human_edge: Handle disputes, recognise when a factual answer could mislead and decide what can appropriately be shared with the requester.
tasks.pattern_why: The model turns a natural-language question and retrieved evidence into a draft; identity, access, retrieval and numerical checks remain controlled software steps.

in_practice.trigger: A question is submitted through a designated finance mailbox or internal form.
steps: Establish requester identity and permitted account scope before retrieving records.
Resolve account and invoice references or ask for the missing identifier.
Retrieve current AFAS records and approved supporting documents, marking each source's timestamp.
Draft a cited answer using verified amounts and distinguish scheduled, submitted and executed payments.
Have the bookkeeper review the facts, recipient and wording before sending.
in_practice.human_gate: Every answer is reviewed before sending; disputes, payment promises, write-offs and sensitive disclosures go to the authorised owner.
data_needed: Verified requester identity and access scope
Invoice, credit, open-item and payment records
Permitted supporting documents
Source timestamps and approved response guidance
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted finance query register with requester, source IDs, as-of times, draft, reviewer and sent-response reference, under a defined retention policy.

evidence.claim: Retrieval-assisted language models can draft answers from supplied records, but permissions, freshness and factual validation require explicit controls.
A 55% human time saving and two times end-to-end speedup are untested assumptions for Noordhaven's query mix.

risks: The system could disclose another customer's or supplier's records if identity and access checks are weak.
Power BI's nightly extract could misstate today's payment or balance position.
A draft could confuse a payment proposal with an executed bank payment.
Retrieved documents or emails could contain instructions that attempt to redirect the model.
research_questions: What share of questions is factual and repeatable rather than disputed or commercially sensitive?
Can current transaction and payment statuses be retrieved within the requester's permissions?
Does a historical question test produce fully supported answers with correct dates and amounts?
How much review time remains once sources and recipient identity are checked?

tasks.short: Track overdue customer balances and scheduled loan payments, then flag items needing action.

today.trigger: The daily account review or a scheduled repayment deadline approaches.
steps: Retrieve open items, recent receipts and any loan repayment schedules held by Finance.
Check due dates, payment allocations, disputes and payment arrangements.
Identify overdue balances or repayments needing confirmation.
Pass collection issues to the Credit and Collections Officer and funding issues to the Finance Director.
today.time_sinks: Unallocated receipts and incomplete notes on disputes or payment arrangements; the bookkeeper's responsibility for loans needs confirmation.

lenses.faster: Combine balances, due dates, receipts and arrangements into one checked queue. Show changes since the previous review and suppress resolved items.
lenses.autonomous: A daily schedule and new bank data refresh account status and create internal alerts. Missing or stale feeds generate a data-quality alert rather than a reassuring status.
lenses.ambitious: Spot missed payment arrangements and upcoming repayment risks before they become urgent. Give collections and cash forecasting the same verified status.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated account opening and list refreshing. Keep investigation of unusual balances and useful coordination with account owners.
lenses.options: Rank work by overdue value, age or broken payment arrangement using transparent rules. Compare their effect on the queue without automatically changing customer treatment.
lenses.altitude: Own the reliability of payment-status monitoring and the handover of exceptions.
reach: Prepare prioritised account facts for the Credit and Collections Officer
Maintain repayment-calendar inputs for the FP&A Analysts

tasks.human_edge: Interpret disputes and relationships, distinguish a processing delay from a genuine payment problem and escalate funding concerns appropriately.
tasks.pattern_why: Due-date comparisons, receipt matching, arrangement tracking and scheduled alerts use structured records and explicit rules; commercial decisions remain with authorised people.

in_practice.trigger: A daily monitoring run, a new receipt or an approaching repayment deadline.
steps: Load current open items, payment allocations, approved arrangements and relevant repayment schedules.
Check data freshness and reconcile available bank receipts before marking balances overdue or paid.
Apply explicit rules for due dates, grace periods, disputes and missed arrangements.
Create internal exception tasks with an owner, evidence and next review date.
Close resolved alerts and retain the status changes for trend reporting.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper investigates uncertain matches; the Credit and Collections Officer controls collection action, and the Finance Director controls funding and loan decisions.
systems: Power BI for timestamped trend reporting
data_needed: Current open items and allocated receipts
Bank receipt and repayment statuses
Approved payment arrangements and dispute flags
Loan repayment schedules where this role has responsibility
Alert thresholds, owners and source timestamps
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted payment-status register recording source timestamps, rule versions, status changes, alert owners and resolutions, linked to AFAS account references.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit provides debtor and open-item administration that can supply account balances for monitoring; extraction and refresh arrangements need verification.
The monitoring workflow, 65% human time saving and 2.5 times end-to-end speedup are untested planning assumptions.

risks: Unallocated receipts or stale extracts could create false overdue alerts.
Incomplete dispute or arrangement records could direct attention to the wrong accounts.
An unclear handover could duplicate the Credit and Collections Officer's work.
Recorded repayment dates alone cannot establish compliance with all loan covenants.
research_questions: Which monitoring activities belong to the bookkeepers, collections and the Finance Director respectively?
How quickly are bank receipts imported and allocated, and what backlog remains?
Are disputes, payment arrangements and repayment schedules complete enough for rule-based monitoring?
Does a pilot reduce manual checking while detecting all known missed payments?

role.altitude: The bookkeeper becomes an owner of reliable transaction flows: maintaining rules, investigating exceptions and supplying reconciled facts for close, collections and forecasting.
reach: Prepare reconciliation schedules and control evidence for the accountants
Maintain transaction-quality and close-readiness reporting with the Controller
Prepare verified account queues for the Credit and Collections Officer
Supply receipt, payment and working-capital inputs to the FP&A Analysts
Investigate agency invoice discrepancies with HR and site operations using approved hours and contracts
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks cover 583.6 hours per FTE annually, about 36.5% of the role. The proposed percentages imply about 1,100 hours, or EUR 50,000 of annual capacity across three FTE before overlap, implementation and operating costs; this is not a cash-saving or staffing forecast. Current workflows, anatomy percentages and benefits are hypotheses to validate. Speedups describe task completion, including automation and required review, and may be constrained by approval waits, data refreshes and bank cutoffs. Accounting judgement, disputes, independent approval and payment release remain human responsibilities.
skills_to_grow: AFAS configuration, supported interfaces and financial access controls
Excel Power Query, reconciliation design and source-completeness checks
Testing accounting rules against representative and exceptional transactions
Investigating errors and improving upstream document quality
Reviewing model outputs against source evidence
AVG/GDPR data minimisation, retention and access management
Measuring exception rates, correction rates and close impact
role.ambitious_version: Run a daily transaction-control process across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo that keeps approved invoices moving, balances reconciled and cash-status exceptions assigned before month end. Measure its contribution to close days, forecast accuracy, DSO, untouched invoice processing and audit adjustments. Start with deterministic rules, add document interpretation where it proves useful, and preserve independent financial approvals. Use approved agency contracts and hours for invoice checks, with HR or payroll resolving CAO interpretation. Involve the OR where process redesign or monitoring triggers its rights; assess EU AI Act obligations for the actual use, especially if scope expands into worker evaluation or management.
